caption: Robust to two people at any gap: lock-v7 with the outer plate rows four blocks out from the inner ones. The door now opens in 2 gt, and the lock waits 12 gt after the outer plates let go. The last inner plate always lets go, and the door has closed, before the lock can catch the door open, and a single person standing in the doorway is still caught open. A repeater halfway along the far row's long dust run keeps its signal alive.
lock-v8 with the lock torch's base beside the near outer row: the torch hangs on it, and the row's dust turns once to feed it through the 2 gt repeater. Two blocks fewer, the same timings.

Tripwire outer rows: tripwire re-checks every 10 gt where a plate re-checks every 20, so the rows can sit 3 blocks from the inner plates, with the lock at 18 gt. The right hooks' blocks feed the lock torch's base under the floor. Robust to two people at any gap, in a shorter box.

The fewest blocks: lock-v10 with the two tripwire rows joined by one dust line beside the door at the walkway's floor level. It runs right under the right hooks' blocks, which power the dust below them, so no wiring under the floor and no blocks to stop dust climbing where it must not.

Opens as you walk up, closes behind you, from either side: one stone plate in front of and behind each door column, the plates' supports wired under the floor into the torches that hold classic6's pistons closed. 44 blocks, no waiting even at a sprint. Stand still in the doorway and the door closes on you and hurts you (half a heart per hurt) until you step out. A mob on a plate opens it too: nothing vanilla tells a player from a mob, so put the plates where mobs can't walk. If the entrance doesn't need to be hidden, two iron doors with plates do the job in about 10 blocks.
